samples.summary: The chip's offline call-to-action fires on the share-link route the design excludes, promising persistence that can never happen there. `offerOffline = stranded && supportsClientKey() && !offlineEnabled` consults neither the identity nor the `not-permitted` lapse. `SharedHeaderStatus` (shared-header-status.tsx:26) renders `SyncStatusChip` for every editor-role share-link visitor, and `shared-document.tsx` wraps the route in `NonDurableScope`, so this document can never be durable. An anonymous visitor who strands work gets the chip rendered as a button plus a toast action, and clicking it emits `toast.success('Saving on this device is on', … 'Documents you open from now on keep un-sent changes on this device')` — false for a visitor with no account, and false for this document in every case. This contradicts the design twice: "Anonymous share-link editors" is a stated Non-Goal (offline-local-persistence.md:64), and sync-status-tooltip.ts:31-34 already withholds the `not-permitted` explanation on the reasoning that saying so "would describe the feature to somebody who does not have it" — the button says it far more loudly. It also cuts against the Goal "the sync chip tells the truth about durability in every case" (line 52). Cost: a user told their unsent work is now kept when nothing is keeping it, on the one route the design decided not to persist.

`OfflineRuntime` is mounted and runs unconditionally, so the "dark launch" property the design claims does not hold. `PrivateRoute` renders it for every signed-in user and the effect gates on nothing — not `useOfflinePersistenceEnabled()`, not `supportsClientKey()`. Every session opens the `wafflebase-offline` IndexedDB database, installs the erase watcher, runs `collectStale()`, and issues an extra `GET /documents` for the revocation reconcile — on a pin (`@yorkie-js/react` 0.7.22, packages/frontend/package.json:66) where `supportsClientKey()` is false and nothing can ever be stored. The design states the opposite twice: "Users who never opt in pay nothing for this feature existing" (offline-local-persistence.md:157) and "nothing changes for anyone until they opt in" (line 540). The cost is bounded — one extra request per session and an empty database per device — but it is a behavior change for 100% of users from a feature nobody can currently turn on.

The design doc names a reuse the implementation does not make, and was not reconciled. § Losing work anyway says "we already have the machinery for it in `DocumentCopyService` / `POST /documents/:id/copy`", and See Also (line 591) lists document-copy.md as "the copy engine the offline-copy recovery path reuses". `offline-copy-recovery.ts` uses neither: it calls `createWorkspaceDocument` plus `applyImportedContent` (the *import* engine) and a bespoke `writeNote`. The choice looks right — the copy service copies a server-side document, while an archive is local bytes whose source may be deleted — but the canonical doc is now the record of an abandoned approach, which is exactly what design-doc discipline exists to prevent. Fold the actual mechanism into the doc rather than leaving the copy-service claim standing.

The implementation deliberately contradicts a rule stated in the design doc added by this same change. offline-local-persistence.md:438 states: "Eligibility may therefore rise mid-session (nothing holds the name yet, so taking it denies nobody) and never falls." `use-durable-document.ts` latches eligibility in *both* directions (`if (latched.current?.identity !== identity) { latched.current = { identity, eligible: eligibleNow } }`), and use-durable-document.test.tsx's "takes no election it will never use when it is switched on" asserts a rise is ignored. The in-code reasoning is persuasive (a rise takes a lock no client is mounted on, and un-settles the hook), so the code is probably the better answer — but the design doc still publishes the rule the code refuses to follow. One of the two has to move.

The offline-transition toast promised for the durable case is absent. offline-local-persistence.md:489 lists two consequences that "follow automatically": the `beforeunload` guard is suppressed when durable (implemented — `mayHaveUnsent` is false in `saved-locally`), "and the offline-transition toast changes from 'keep this tab open' to 'saved to this device'". The toast effect keys on `stranded`, i.e. `state === 'not-saved'` only, so a durable document going offline emits no toast at all rather than a reworded one. Silence is defensible, but it is not what the doc specifies and the user gets no confirmation at the moment the feature is doing its job.
searchedFor: toast.warning / toast.success call sites in sync-status-chip.tsx

samples.summary: The recovery message does not name which of the three drop reasons applied. offline-local-persistence.md:523: "The user is then told what happened, **in the vocabulary of the three reasons**, with a link to the copy." `DurableLossWatch` subscribes to `local-changes-dropped` and discards the event payload (`() => { durable.store.expectLoss(doc.getKey()); durable.reportLoss(); }`), nothing persists a reason alongside the archive, and the offer toast is the generic "Edits to \"X\" could not be reconciled with the server." for all three of `epoch-reanchor`, `document-purged` and `actor-mismatch`. The link to the copy is implemented; the vocabulary is not. The Goal (work returned as a document) still holds, so the cost is explanatory rather than functional.

Two further doc statements describe behavior the store does not implement. (1) § Layout and migration (lines 245-251) specifies "An `onupgradeneeded` that relocates each existing value into the snapshot store, with an empty change log beside it, is the whole migration"; `wafflebase-doc-store.ts`'s upgrade handler only creates the stores and comments "Version 1 creates; there is nothing in the wild to migrate" — correct, and it makes the doc paragraph describe a migration that neither exists nor is needed. (2) The cleanup table (line 281) calls the 30-day sweep "Periodic"; `OfflineRuntime` runs `collectStale()` exactly once per session and argues in comments why a timer would be wrong. Both small, but the canonical doc should state what shipped.

`TYPE_PREFIXES` adds a third home for the document-type↔docKey prefix mapping. The forward direction already lives in `apply-imported-content.ts`'s `buildDocKey` (sheet/doc/slides/board) and in the inline template literals each detail route uses (`note-${id}` at notes-detail.tsx:378, shared-document.tsx:1001); `use-durable-document.ts`'s `isExcluded` encodes the `pdf-` half separately. This file encodes the reverse mapping again. No shared helper exists (`grep 'export function buildDocKey|docKeyFor'` finds nothing), so the duplication predates this change — but this new copy is the one that decides whether an archive is recoverable at all, so a document type added to `buildDocKey` without a matching entry here would leave that type's archived work silently unoffered. A single exported prefix table in frontend `lib/` would collapse all of them.

`writeNote` re-implements the note root rather than reusing the existing constructor, against an explicitly documented rule. `types/notes-document.ts` exports `initialNotesRoot()` (line 46) as the canonical note root and warns at the top of the file, in capitals, that `Text` must come from `@yorkie-js/react` and never `@yorkie-js/sdk` because the classes have different identities. `writeNote` imports `Text` from `@yorkie-js/sdk` (line 1) and builds `root.content = new Text()` by hand inside `doc.update`, attaching with no `initialRoot` at all — unlike every branch of `applyImportedContent`, which seeds with the type's own initial root. Whether the `instanceof` hazard bites here is the correctness lens's call; the duplication is the fit issue: the file that owns the note root says "Do NOT add fields to this root without treating it as a migration event", and a second construction site is how that gets broken.

The Rollout table's PR split is not what landed. PRs 2 (the store), 3 (per-document client + app lock, "still passing no store"), 4 (wiring, opt-in, chip, recovery) and 5 (revise sync-status.md) all appear in this one change — `wafflebase-doc-store.ts`, `durable-session.ts`, `use-durable-document.ts`, `offline-runtime.tsx` and the sync-status.md revision are all new here. The doc's stated reason for splitting was "so that a regression in either is unambiguous"; shipping them together forfeits that, and the table should be corrected so it is not read as a record of how this shipped.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. sync-status-chip.tsx:85 computes `offerOffline = stranded && supportsClientKey() && !offlineEnabled` with no reference to the `not-permitted` lapse it already reads at line 78, and renders the CTA as both a button (226-240) and a toast action (177-181) whose handler claims 'Documents you open from now on keep un-sent changes on this device' (93-96). That path is reachable on the share route: shared-header-status.tsx:18-26 renders SyncStatusChip for every editor-role visitor, and shared-document.tsx:317/393/443/526/652 sit inside NonDurableScope (1016,1092), which use-durable-document.ts:61-70,122-132 turns into permanently non-durable (permitted=false, plus !!userId for anonymous); collab-document-provider.tsx:295-296 publishes `not-permitted` for exactly this case. This contradicts the governing design doc twice: offline-local-persistence.md:64-65 makes 'Anonymous share-link editors' a Non-Goal and line 52 states the Goal that the chip 'tells the truth about durability in every case'; sync-status-tooltip.ts:24-27 (and the test at sync-status-chip.test.tsx:679-685) deliberately withholds the `not-permitted` sentence to avoid 'describ[ing] the feature to somebody who does not have it', while the button does so far more loudly. I considered refuting on already-guarded via supportsClientKey() (yorkie-capabilities.ts:76-82), but that pin gate is a global dark-launch switch the design says is lifted by a single dependency bump (offline-local-persistence.md:555-565), not a route-specific guard, so it does not make this unreachable. Cost is user-facing — an anonymous share-link visitor is told unsent work is now kept when nothing keeps it — which is major, not tidiness, under this lens.

finding.summary: Swallowing a failed `doc.subscribe` leaves `durable` true, breaking the design's "durable ⇒ reportable" / under-promise rule — and, for the loss event, also breaks archive-on-remove
finding.evidence: The new `watch()` helper catches a throwing `subscribe` and only `console.warn`s; nothing flips the durability state. `docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md` states the invariant explicitly: "Durable-but-unreportable is worse than uniformly non-durable: it is a guarantee the user cannot see, check, or be warned about when it lapses" (§ Who gets it) and "A failure the store cannot classify still flips `durable` — the default is to under-promise" (§ What the user sees). After a swallowed failure the chip keeps reading `Saved to this device` for a document whose `PersistDisabled`/`LocalChangesDropped` can never be reported. Worse, the comment's claim that this "costs the chip its certainty, never the document" does not hold for the first subscription: per § Storage, `WafflebaseDocStore.remove()` archives only what `expectLoss` latched (`wafflebase-doc-store.ts:739,757`), and the SDK calls `remove` on every detach — so if the `local-changes-dropped` subscription silently fails, unreconciled work is deleted instead of archived, defeating the Goal "Work that genuinely cannot be reconciled with the server is returned to the user as a document." The safe shape the design asks for is to latch durability off (a lapse reason) when a required durability event cannot be watched, rather than to continue silently.

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as the reviewer describes. `watch()` in durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:269-278 swallows a throwing `subscribe` with only a console.warn and changes no state; `durable` (line 181) is `!lost && !writesFailing && !persistDisabled`, and a repo-wide grep shows `reportLoss`/`reportPersistDisabled` are invoked only from inside the two subscription callbacks (lines 283, 294) — so no guard anywhere flips durability when a subscription cannot be established. That contradicts the design's explicit invariants at docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md:102-107 ("durable ⇒ reportable"; durable-but-unreportable is worse than non-durable) and :486-487 ("A failure the store cannot classify still flips `durable` — the default is to under-promise"). The second, heavier consequence also checks out: wafflebase-doc-store.ts:739-741 latches `expectedLosses` solely from the `local-changes-dropped` handler, and `remove()` archives only when `losing` is true (:771, :791-803), deleting outright otherwise (:809-811) — while the SDK calls `remove` on every ordinary detach (:726-729, design :258-270). So a silently failed loss subscription turns a loss path into an outright delete, defeating the stated Goal at design :54-55 that unreconcilable work is returned to the user as a document. I could not establish unreachability: node_modules/@yorkie-js is not present to prove the event names never throw, and the only version gate in the durable path (`supportsClientKey()` in use-durable-document.ts:128, collab-document-provider.tsx:223) concerns the `clientKey` prop, not event support. Under the design-fit rubric this is an acceptance criterion / stated invariant left unmet with a user-visible cost, i.e. major.
